title: Regulatory Uncertainty and Market Volatility: The Impact of AI Governance Frameworks on Algorithmic Trading Strategies
abstract: We examine how evolving AI regulation and policy uncertainty affect market volatility and the behavior of algorithmic trading systems in equity and derivatives markets. Using a panel dataset spanning 14 jurisdictions over 2019-2024, we find that periods of high regulatory uncertainty — defined as elevated frequency of AI governance announcements without enacted legislation — are associated with a statistically significant 18-23% increase in intraday volatility across AI-exposed sectors. We further show that institutional trading algorithms undergo measurable strategy shifts during these periods, reducing exposure to high-AI-intensity stocks. Our findings suggest that regulatory intervention timelines and communication clarity are first-order determinants of market stability in AI-driven financial ecosystems. We discuss policy implications for central banks and securities regulators seeking to minimize market disruption during AI governance transitions.
